bitstream_source: main's Verilog, 67386afb's, by make -C icepi in CI's release dry run 42384444259 (icepi-zero-v1.4.bit), for an Icepi Zero v1.3
firmware_sha256: of each python/bench_firmware.py entry as sorted, compact JSON, or of the test/ file, at the run's commit
bench: an Icepi Zero (ECP5 LFE5U-25F) running the chip at 48 MHz on bench carrier v1.2, Pico A as the host on SPI, nothing, Pico B idle on OUT0, analyser A (fx2lafw) at 24 MS/s
scope: the bytes on the wire and their timing in one run of dmx512, as the analyser saw them
limits: one run of one board, the ECP5 build of the chip's RTL, not the ASIC
the run's files are the bench's own record, tied together by SHA256SUMS, and CI derives the decode and the timing from the capture alone
each edge is known to a sample either way and the analyser's crystal to 100 ppm, and a window the capture cannot settle is unresolved, not passed

the bitstream is named by its sha256, built from main's Verilog, 67386afb's, by make -C icepi in CI's release dry run 42384444259 (icepi-zero-v1.4.bit), for an Icepi Zero v1.3 by the bench's notes, which CI does not rebuild
sealed on the held-out list and written blind from its spec (docs/flexibility.md)
the page gives 250 kbit/s no tolerance, which a sample either way can't settle, so each low is also held to the firmware's bit within half a bit over nine
the first packet reads misframed, as the line is low from reset, so the bytes are the second's
